1.1: Paul and Timothy, bondservants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with the bishops and deacons:
1.2: Grace and peace to y'all from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: I thank my God every time I think of y'all,
1.4: Always, in every prayer, I'm making requests for you all with joy,
1.5: For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now,
1.6: Being confident of this: that He who started a good work in you will finish it until the day of Christ Jesus.
1.7: It's right for me to think this way about all of you, 'cause I got y'all in my heart. Even though I'm in chains, and defending and confirming the gospel, you're all partakers of this grace with me.
1.8: For God is my witness, how much I long for all of you with the affection of Jesus Christ.
1.9: And this is what I pray: that your love may keep growing more and more, with knowledge and discernment,
1.10: So you can approve the things that are excellent, and be sincere and without offense until the day of Christ,
1.11: Filled with the fruits of righteousness that come through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
1.12: Now, I want y'all to know, that everything that's happened to me has actually helped spread the gospel,
1.13: So much so, that it's become clear to the whole palace guard, and to everyone else, that my chains are for Christ,
1.14: And most of the believers in the Lord, having seen my chains, have become more confident and are preaching the word without fear.
1.15: Some are preaching Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others are doing it out of goodwill.
1.16: The ones doing it out of rivalry are doing it for selfish reasons, thinking they're adding trouble to my chains,
1.17: But the ones doing it out of love know that I'm here for the defense of the gospel.
1.18: So, what's the deal? As long as Christ is preached, whether it's out of a fake act or real love, I'm good with it. I rejoice, and I'll keep rejoicing.
1.19: For I know this will turn out for my deliverance because of your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
1.20: According to my earnest expectation and hope, that I won't be ashamed, but with boldness—just like always—Christ will be magnified in my body, whether I live or die.
1.21: For me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
1.22: But if I keep living, that'll mean more fruit from my labor; yet, honestly, I don't know which to choose.
1.23: I'm stuck between the two: I wanna go be with Christ, 'cause that's way better,
1.24: But to stay here is more needed for you.
1.25: I'm confident that I'm gonna stay and keep helping y'all grow in your faith,
1.26: So y'all can rejoice even more when I get back to you in Christ.
1.27: Only let your conduct be worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come to see you or stay away, I'll hear about your affairs—that you stand firm in one spirit, striving together with one mind for the faith of the gospel,
1.28: And don't be intimidated by your enemies—when they're scared, that's a sign of their defeat, but for you, it's a sign of your salvation, and that comes from God.
1.29: For to you, it's been granted not just to believe in Christ, but also to suffer for His sake,
1.30: Having the same struggle you saw in me, and now hear about in me.

2.1: So, if there's any encouragement in Christ, if there's any comfort in love, if there's any fellowship in the Spirit, if there's any affection and mercy,
2.2: Then make my joy complete by being like-minded, having the same love, being united, and thinking the same way.
2.3: Don't do stuff out of selfish ambition or pride, but in humility, consider others better than yourself.
2.4: Don't just look out for your own interests, but for the interests of others too.
2.5: Let this mindset be in you, the same as it was in Christ Jesus,
2.6: Who, being in the form of God, didn't think it was stealing to be equal with God,
2.7: But He emptied Himself, took on the form of a servant, and came in the likeness of man.
2.8: And when He showed up as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to the point of death, even the death on the cross.
2.9: Therefore, God has highly exalted Him and given Him the name that's above every name,
2.10: That at the name of Jesus, every knee should bow—whether in heaven, on earth, or under the earth,
2.11: And every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
2.12: So, my beloved, as you've always obeyed, not only when I was around, but even more now that I'm not, Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling;
2.13: 'Cause it's God who's working in you, helping you to want what's right and to do what pleases Him.
2.14: Do everything without complaining or arguing,
2.15: So that you'll be blameless and innocent, children of God without fault in this crooked and messed-up generation,
2.16: Among whom you shine as lights in the world, holding onto the word of life, So that when Christ comes back, I'll have reason to rejoice, knowing I didn't waste my time or labor.
2.17: And if I'm being poured out as a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I'm glad and I rejoice with you all.
2.18: And y'all should be glad and rejoice with me too.
2.19: But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I can be encouraged when I know how you're doing.
2.20: I don't have anyone else like him, who will genuinely care for your situation,
2.21: 'Cause everyone else is focused on their own stuff, not the things that matter to Christ Jesus.
2.22: But you know his proven character—he served with me like a son with his father, in spreading the gospel.
2.23: So, I'm hoping to send him as soon as I see how things go with me.
2.24: But I trust the Lord that I'll come to you myself soon too.
2.25: I thought it was necessary to send Epaphroditus back to you—my brother, my coworker, my soldier—he's your messenger and the one who helped me in my need,
2.26: Since he was missing y'all and was worried that you heard he was sick.
2.27: He was sick almost to the point of death, but God showed mercy on him—and not just on him, but on me too, so I wouldn't have sorrow on top of sorrow.
2.28: So, I'm sending him back to you even more eagerly, so when you see him again, you can rejoice, and I'll be a little less sorrowful.
2.29: Receive him with joy in the Lord, and hold men like him in high regard,
2.30: 'Cause he came close to death for the work of Christ, not worrying about his own life, to make up for what was lacking in your service to me.

3.1: Finally, my people, rejoice in the Lord. For me to write the same thing to you ain't no big deal, but for you, it's safe.
3.2: Watch out for them dogs, watch out for them evil workers, watch out for the ones who be cutting themselves!
3.3: We the real deal—circumcised in the Spirit, worshiping God, rejoicing in Christ Jesus, and not putting any trust in the flesh.
3.4: But if anyone thinks they got reason to boast in the flesh, I got even more reason:
3.5: Circumcised on the eighth day, from the tribe of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as far as the law goes, I was a Pharisee;
3.6: I had so much zeal, I was out here persecuting the church; and when it came to the righteousness from the law, I was blameless.
3.7: But all that stuff I thought was gain? I count it as loss for Christ.
3.8: Actually, I count everything as loss compared to the greatness of knowing Christ Jesus, my Lord. I lost everything for Him, and I count it as trash, so I can gain Christ.
3.9: And be found in Him, not with my own righteousness that comes from the law, but with the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ—the righteousness that's from God, by faith.
3.10: I wanna know Him, and I want to experience the power of His resurrection, and share in His sufferings, becoming like Him in His death,
3.11: If by any means, I can reach the resurrection from the dead.
3.12: I'm not saying I've already reached it, or that I'm already perfect, but I press on to grab what Christ Jesus grabbed me for.
3.13: Brothers and sisters, I don't count myself as having gotten there yet, but one thing I do: I forget what's behind and I'm reaching for what's ahead.
3.14: I press toward the goal for the prize of the high call of God in Christ Jesus.
3.15: So, if you're mature, let's think like this; and if you disagree with me on anything, God will show you what's right.
3.16: But until then, let's walk the same way we've been walking, thinking the same thing.
3.17: Brothers and sisters, follow my example, and look at those who walk the way we walk, 'cause we gave you a pattern to follow.
3.18: There's a lot of people out here walking the wrong way, and I've told y'all before, and I'm even crying about it now. They're enemies of the cross of Christ,
3.19: Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and they're out here glorifying their shame—focused on earthly things.
3.20: But our citizenship is in heaven, and we're waiting for the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
3.21: Who will transform our lowly bodies, so that they can be like His glorious body, by the power He has to make everything submit to Himself.

4.1: Therefore, my beloved and longed-for brothers and sisters, my joy and crown, so stand firm in the Lord, beloved.
4.2: I'm begging Euodia and Syntyche to get on the same page in the Lord.
4.3: And I urge you, true companion, help these women who worked with me in the gospel, with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the Book of Life.
4.4: Rejoice in the Lord always. Again, I say, rejoice!
4.5: Let your gentleness be known to everyone. The Lord is near.
4.6: Don't worry about anything, but in everything, through prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be known to God,
4.7: And the peace of God, which passes all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
4.8: Finally, my people, whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable—if there's any excellence or anything worthy of praise—think on these things.
4.9: The things you learned, received, heard, and saw in me, do them, and the God of peace will be with you.
4.10: I'm so happy in the Lord that now, at last, your care for me has blossomed again. You were always concerned, but you didn't have the chance before.
4.11: Not that I'm in need—I've learned to be content in whatever state I'm in.
4.12: I know what it's like to be low, and I know what it's like to have plenty. I've learned how to be full and how to be hungry, how to have more than enough and how to need.
4.13: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
4.14: But you did well by sharing in my struggles.
4.15: You Philippians know that in the beginning of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church helped me with giving and receiving but you only.
4.16: Even when I was in Thessalonica, y'all sent me help more than once.
4.17: Not that I'm chasing the gift, but I'm chasing the fruit that's growing in your account.
4.18: I've got everything I need and more. I'm full, having received from Epaphroditus what you sent me, a sweet-smelling gift, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.
4.19: And my God will meet all your needs according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
4.20: Now to our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
4.21: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters here with me send their greetings to you.
4.22: All the saints send their greetings, especially those from Caesar's household.
4.23: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
